sentence: The intervals divide each estimate by $1+\beta$, where $\beta$ is the relative closure bias at nominal truth, and add the standard error of $\beta$ times the corrected estimate in quadrature to the statistical standard deviation. A quantity fails when the upper confidence bound on its coverage lies below 0.66 for 68\% intervals or below 0.94 for 95\% intervals. Each bound uses the Bonferroni level of Fig.~\ref{fig:coverage-5d-paper}, one correction over the 153 integrals and the three generated truths. The 68\% assessment and the 95\% assessment are separate; each uses that level.

The second truth (the $\Eavail$ tilt) multiplies the true signal by $1+0.2\,(\Eavail/\SI{100}{GeV}-\tfrac12)$ without renormalization, with the background unchanged; below $\Eavail=\SI{3}{GeV}$ the weight is 0.900--0.906.
